description: tab:prelowering controlled measurement, 2026-08-24. Uniform two-arm protocol: arm A (No Pre-Opt) = flat expand path (DEBUG_PROBPROG_DISABLE_OPT=true) + disable_licm_optimization_passes=true; arm B (Pre-Opt) = flat expand path + full standard passes. SICM off in both arms. 20 NUTS samples, adaptation off, CPU, median of 5 runs per cell after 1 warm-up call, no thread caps.
machine: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 7995WX, 96 cores / 192 threads, 1 NUMA node

ir_evidence.method: ablation/pre_lowering/analyze_ir.py classifies ops by stablehlo.while nesting depth. depth 0 = top level (InitHMC gradient), depth 1 = NUTS sampling while (and the InitHMC gradient's own model time loop), depth 3 = per leapfrog step outside the model time loop, depth 4 = innermost model time loop.

Cubic Kernel (both sizes).reading: arm A keeps 3 O(D^3) matmuls in the innermost time loop (forward K construction + 2 reverse-pass instances) and 3 more in the InitHMC gradient's time loop; arm B has zero at either time-loop depth, with the same 3+3 hoisted one while-level out. The time loop retains only the O(D^2) 1xD @ DxD state updates in both arms.

Projected Dynamics.metric: D x D elementwise/shape ops (the K = theta*A + I construction) by while-depth
Projected Dynamics.reading: no O(D^3) dot_general exists in either arm (the invariant is an O(D^2) elementwise construction, which is why this row's speedup is the smallest). Arm A rebuilds K inside the time loop every step; arm B keeps only the loop-carried Kbar accumulate (one DxD add) there.

Heat Equation (D=100).metric: LAPACK custom_calls by result signature and while-depth
Heat Equation (D=100).reading: 22 potrf total in arm A, 20 of them inside the time loops; 2 total in arm B, 0 in the time loops. dtrsm stays in the time loops in both arms, as it must. Reproduces heat_inverse_RESULTS_2026-08-21.md exactly on the current binary.

ir_evidence.syevd: 0 in every measured cell of every batch (SICM-off proof)
